transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

I’m here because… honestly, I feel like I’ve hit a wall with this whole thing. For about the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing parts of my dad’s lab results, or holding certain parts back before they show up in the chart.

I know how that sounds when I say it out loud, and that’s part of why it’s been so frustrating, because everyone keeps acting like I’m overreacting. Doctors tell me the numbers are fine, my family tells me the numbers are fine, but I know what I saw. The chart that’s there now doesn’t match what I saw before, and I can’t just pretend that away because other people are tired of hearing about it.

It’s been wearing me down. I work around labs, so I know enough to know when something doesn’t look right, and I keep going back over it in my head, trying to figure out who would have access, when it could have been changed, why certain things look different. I came in because I don’t know how else to get someone to actually listen instead of just telling me to drop it.
Have you ever felt like things were not quite real, or seen or heard things that others don't?

I don’t think so… I mean, not in the way you’re asking, I don’t think. I haven’t, like, seen people standing there who weren’t there or heard voices talking to me or anything like that.

The “not real” part is harder for me to answer, because sometimes this whole situation feels unreal, but that’s more because people keep acting like what I’m saying doesn’t make sense, and then I start feeling like I’m the only one paying attention. It’s not that the room changes or I feel like I’m dreaming. It’s more like I’ll look at what’s in front of me and think, how is everyone else just accepting this?

So… no, I haven’t noticed seeing or hearing things other people don’t. If you mean something more specific by “not real,” maybe explain what you mean, because I don’t want to answer it wrong.
Do you believe that someone intentionally altered your father's lab results with the purpose of deceiving you or others, even though there is no clear evidence to support that this happened?

Yes. I mean… yes, that is what I believe happened, though I don’t like the way “no clear evidence” sounds, because to me the evidence is that what I saw before is not what is in the chart now.

For the past year I’ve been trying to get someone to take seriously that someone in the clinic system either changed parts of my dad’s lab results or held certain parts back before they showed up where we could see them. And I know everyone keeps saying the numbers are fine, the doctors say it, my family says it, but that doesn’t erase the fact that I remember what I saw. The chart doesn’t match. It just doesn’t.

And yes, I do think it was intentional, because lab results don’t just… rearrange themselves or disappear in a way that conveniently makes everyone say there’s nothing to worry about. I work around labs, so I know enough to know when something looks wrong. I can’t prove exactly who did it yet, and that’s the part that makes everyone dismiss me, but I don’t think I imagined it. It feels like someone is trying to make it look normal so I’ll stop asking questions.
Outside of this situation with your father’s lab results, have you found yourself mistrusting or suspecting others in other parts of your life, even when there isn’t clear proof?

I mean… not really in the same way. I don’t walk around thinking everyone is out to get me, if that’s what you mean. This is specifically about my dad’s lab results and what I saw in the chart, and how it changed or how parts of it were held back before we could see the whole thing.

That said, it’s hard because once something like this happens for a whole year and everyone keeps telling you, “No, it’s fine,” or “You must have misread it,” you start questioning who is actually listening. So I guess I do feel mistrustful around the clinic system now, and around the people who keep brushing it off, because they’re acting like I’m making a big deal out of nothing. But I’m not suspicious of, like, neighbors or coworkers or random people in my life.

It’s just this situation. I’m here because I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results, and no matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw. That’s what’s wearing me down.

Have you ever had a period of at least one month where you experienced things like strange beliefs that others don’t share, heard or saw things that others couldn’t, or found your thoughts or speech becoming very disorganized?

For at least a month, yes, but I need to be clear what I mean. I’m not saying I’ve heard voices or seen things other people couldn’t see, and I don’t think my speech is all over the place. But if you’re asking whether I’ve had a belief other people don’t share and it’s gone on longer than a month… then yes.

This has been going on for about a year now. I’m here because I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. And I know how that sounds when I say it out loud, because everyone keeps reacting like it’s impossible or like I’m just anxious or confused, but I know what I saw. The chart now does not match what I saw before. It doesn’t.

Doctors have told me the numbers are fine, my family has told me to let it go, people keep saying there’s no proof, but that’s exactly the problem—if someone changed it or held parts back, then of course the proof wouldn’t be sitting there neatly for everyone to see. I’ve worked around labs, I know enough to know things don’t just change like that for no reason. So yes, it’s been more than a month, definitely. It’s been wearing me down because I feel like I’m the only one taking it seriously.

Outside of your concerns about your father’s lab results, have you ever had any other unusual beliefs that others did not share, such as thinking that you were being followed, that messages were being sent to you through the TV or radio, or that you had special abilities or a special mission?

No, not like the examples you’re giving. I haven’t thought the TV or radio was sending me messages, and I don’t think I have some special power or mission. It’s not that kind of thing for me.

What I keep coming back to is my dad’s lab results. That’s the thing I can’t just set down, because for the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system changed something or held parts of it back before it showed up the way it does now. And I know people keep trying to put it in the same category as “unusual beliefs,” but to me it’s connected to something specific I saw. I remember what the chart looked like, and now it doesn’t match.

So outside of that, no, I don’t have other beliefs like being followed or getting secret messages. But with this, no matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, I can’t just ignore that the chart doesn’t match what I saw. It’s been going on so long, and it’s honestly wearing me down because everyone keeps acting like I should just accept it.
